items.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: Yesterday was a string quartet of all jazz string players. Violins. And Skitch Henderson was on piano. And Peter Appleyard, and a lady bass player, Nicki Parrott, and Joe Ascione and Bucky Pizzarelli.

ctx.x: Two days in a row really. Yesterday was a string quartet of all jazz string players. Violins. And Skitch Henderson was on piano. And Peter Appleyard, and a lady bass player, Nicki Parrott, and Joe Ascione and Bucky Pizzarelli. And it was for label called Arbors Records.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So I didn’t want to get in on that so Gene Bertoncini quit the show and they asked me to do it with Skitch Henderson

ctx.x: Yeah. And then the set groups were playing now. They weren’t using studio guys. Record companies turned over the studios to a group. Now the group would sit around all day long trying to make a track. A rhythm track. And nobody could get in — Mitch Miller couldn’t get into his own studios down there because some group was sitting there trying to make rhythm tracks, and they’re subtracting and adding — take this out, put this in— waste of time. Big waste of time and money. So I didn’t want to get in on that so…
And what was the schedule like for that show?
